items.title: Al Rose Interview, 1975-02-03
items.q: Bob Green is compelled, and he has to get his practice in every day or he gets nervous.

ctx.x: Oh yeah, well, Naki was writing his dissertation at my place in Key Largo. He was down there for two months, and Naki virtually never touched the piano in that time, although he had time to do it in.
But some people are compelled to play that. Well, he's not one. Bob Green is compelled,

and he has to get his practice in every day or he gets nervous. And of course, the thing that he's doing is so extremely demanding that I can imagine that it doesn't take much to get out of practice with the business of trying to reproduce literally the sound of Jelly Roll Morton. He works with that variable speed tape recorder, which he regulates the speed of to provide the right pitch. Then he plays the Jelly Roll records, and then he plays the piano, you see. And he's never through until you can only hear one…
